questions.subject: maths8
questions.q: Consider the figure given below, showing a solid with a triangular front and back face joined by a rectangular base, top ridge, and two rectangular side faces (a tent-shaped solid). What is the name of the above figure?
questions.explanation: A solid with two parallel triangular faces connected by rectangular faces is a triangular prism.

questions.subject: maths8
questions.q: The figure given below is a right circular cylinder with a radius of 7cm and a height of 13cm. What is the surface area of the cylinder? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr(r + h) = 2π(7)(7+13) = 2π(7)(20) = 280π cm².

questions.subject: maths8
questions.q: The figure given below is a right rectangular prism with a length of 4cm, a width of 0.5cm and a height of 3cm. What is the volume of the prism?
questions.explanation: Volume of a rectangular prism = length × width × height = 4 × 0.5 × 3 = 6 cm³.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following indigenous methods of measurement is used to measure time?
questions.explanation: Sunrise and sunset is a traditional, indigenous way people have measured/marked time, unlike the other standardized modern time units listed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Among the following, one is NOT the correct explanation of the components of scientific method.
options: A hypothesis is a critical look through natural world.
Experimentation is the process of testing our hypothesis using the collected data.
Analysis is the process of studying the organized material in order to discover the essential facts.
A theory is a tested explanation of hypothesis and facts.
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is actually a tentative, testable explanation or prediction — not "a critical look through the natural world" (that description fits observation instead).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following sets of physical quantities are all fundamental quantities?
questions.explanation: Time, length, mass, and current are all fundamental (basic) physical quantities; volume, area, and pressure are derived quantities calculated from combinations of fundamental ones.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the name of the prefix that we use to write 1.0 x 10⁻⁶ seconds without exponent?
questions.explanation: The prefix micro (μ) represents 10⁻⁶, so 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ seconds is written as 1.0 microsecond.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Masantu is a grade eight student and she is given instruments like watch, meter and measuring cylinder. What can Masantu measure among the following respectively?
questions.explanation: A watch measures time, a meter (metre stick) measures length, and a measuring cylinder measures volume.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is TRUE about basic and derived physical quantities?
options: Volume is a basic physical quantity whereas Mass is a derived physical quantity.
The units of all derived physical quantities are derived from units of basic quantities.
The SI units are used only to express the units of basic quantities.
Kilometer is the SI unit of basic unit whereas meter is the SI unit of derived unit.
questions.explanation: Derived physical quantities (like volume, speed, or density) have units built from combinations of the units of basic quantities (like length, mass, and time).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The electric charge and the relative approximate mass of a neutron, respectively, are
questions.explanation: A neutron has no electric charge (zero) and a relative mass of approximately one atomic mass unit, similar to a proton.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following statement correctly describes the structure of an atom?
options: The nucleus of an atom is a dense central part of an atom
Protons revolve in shell around the nucleus of an atom
Protons and neutrons are found around the nucleus of an atom
The region occupied by electron is very large compared with the size of the nucleus.
questions.explanation: The nucleus is indeed the small, dense central part of the atom, containing the protons and neutrons, while electrons occupy the surrounding shells/orbitals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom is--------------, and the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom is ---------
options: mass number and number of electron.
atomic weight and number of electron.
number of neutron and atomic number.
questions.explanation: The number of protons alone is the atomic number, while the total of protons plus neutrons is the mass number.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in the atom of ⁶³₂₉Cu, respectively?
questions.explanation: Protons = atomic number = 29; neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 63 − 29 = 34; electrons = protons = 29 (neutral atom).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The hydrogen atom with atomic number, Z = 1, has one electron in its shell and mass number, A = 1. Which one of the following statements correctly describes the hydrogen atom? It has:
questions.explanation: Since the mass number (1) equals the number of protons (1), there are no neutrons (1 − 1 = 0) in this hydrogen atom.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Compounds containing carbon with exception of carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide are classified as ----
questions.explanation: Carbon-containing compounds are classified as organic compounds, with a few historical exceptions (carbonates, hydrogen carbonates, CO, and CO2) that are treated as inorganic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical formula of alkane, alkene and alkyne with seven (7) carbon atoms is---------.
questions.explanation: For 7 carbons: the alkane is C7H16 (CnH2n+2), the alkene is C7H14 (CnH2n), and the alkyne is C7H12 (CnH2n-2).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Among the following alternatives, the compound and its chemical name correctly matched in
questions.explanation: KOH is correctly named potassium hydroxide. H2SO4 is sulfuric acid (not sulfurous), NaOH is sodium hydroxide (not nitrogen hydroxide), and HNO3 is nitric acid (not nitrous acid).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water is known as:
questions.explanation: This reaction between an acid and a base producing salt and water is called neutralization.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following safety precautions is correct while working with acids and bases in school laboratories?
options: Washing the affected part with plenty of water
Washing the concentrated acid splashed area of the skin with strong base
questions.explanation: Washing the affected area with plenty of water is the correct first-aid response; acid should always be added to water (never the reverse), and drinking or neutralizing acid on skin with a strong base are both dangerous.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Identify the true statement about non -metallic oxides.
options: Most non-metallic oxides exhibit acidic properties.
All non-metallic oxides are neutral oxides.
All non-metallic oxides are necessarily acidic oxides.
Water solution of non-metallic oxide gives basic solution.
questions.explanation: Most (though not strictly all — e.g., CO and NO are neutral) non-metallic oxides exhibit acidic properties, ruling out the absolute claims in the other options.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Nonmetallic oxides are formed by burning nonmetallic elements in oxygen. Which one of the following reactions is used to prepare SO2 in your school laboratory?
questions.explanation: Burning sulfur directly in oxygen (S + O2 → SO2) is the standard school-laboratory method to prepare sulfur dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Farmers spread calcium hydroxide on their fields to neutralize soils that are too acidic for crops to grow well. Which ion in calcium hydroxide neutralizes the acid in the soil?
questions.explanation: The hydroxide ion (OH-) from calcium hydroxide reacts with and neutralizes the excess H+ (acid) in the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the function of human integumentary system?
options: Allows us to move in a particular ways.
questions.explanation: The integumentary system (skin) helps regulate body temperature, among its other protective functions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish the true statement about human muscular system.
options: Smooth muscles are capable of permitting body movement.
Skeletal muscles are found in the walls of viscera and blood vessels.
Cardiac muscles are attached to the bones of the skeleton by tendons.
The contraction of smooth and cardiac muscle is involuntary.
questions.explanation: Smooth and cardiac muscles contract involuntarily (without conscious control), unlike skeletal muscles, which are voluntary and attach to bones by tendons.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the main function of human skeletal system?
options: Protects vital organs, such as the heart.
Absorption of digested nutrients to body cells.
questions.explanation: A main function of the skeletal system is to protect vital internal organs, such as the ribcage protecting the heart and lungs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the function of canine teeth in carnivorous animals? It is used for:
questions.explanation: Canine teeth are pointed and designed for tearing flesh, while incisors cut and molars grind/crush food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about female reproductive structures in humans?
options: Cervix: an erectile and sensitive tissue like a penis.
Vagina: it is a site for egg production
Uterus: is a muscular tube serves as birth canal.
Fallopian tube: it is a site for fertilization.
questions.explanation: Fertilization typically occurs in the fallopian tube, where the egg meets sperm; eggs are produced in the ovaries, and the vagina (not the uterus) serves as the birth canal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the primary sexual characteristic in male?
options: Production of sperm cells and sex hormones.
Development of desire to the opposite sex.
Presence of penis, testes, and scrotum.
questions.explanation: The presence of the penis, testes, and scrotum — the reproductive organs themselves — constitutes the primary sexual characteristic in males, distinct from secondary characteristics that develop at puberty.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sexually Transmitted Disease (STD) which is caused by Treponema palladium bacteria is:
questions.explanation: Syphilis is the STD caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which parts of female reproductive system are concerned with egg cell production?
questions.explanation: The ovaries are the organs responsible for producing egg cells (ova) in the female reproductive system.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is true about food web and food chain?
options: Producers are not involved in food chains and food webs.
Carnivorous animals are at the base of any food web.
Both food chain and food web are complex feeding relationships.
Food chain is single linear, while food web is complex feeding relationships.
questions.explanation: A food chain is a single, linear sequence of feeding relationships, while a food web represents the more complex, interconnected feeding relationships among many organisms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The exchange of necessary nutrients between living organisms and non-living world is very important because nutrients are:
questions.explanation: Nutrients are limited/finite in nature, so their continuous cycling and exchange between living organisms and the non-living environment is essential to sustain life.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which soil type would be good for making pottery?
questions.explanation: Clay soil, due to its fine particles and moldable, plastic texture when wet, is well suited for making pottery.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following method is used to conserve soil?
questions.explanation: Crop rotation helps conserve soil fertility and structure, unlike overgrazing, deforestation, or fossil fuel burning, which degrade soil and the environment.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In nature water provides all the following functions, EXCEPT:
options: producing food in plants by photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Water plays a natural role in regulating body temperature, generating hydroelectric power, and photosynthesis — but it has no natural role in "developing the electronics industry," making that the exception.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT the impact of air pollution? It:
questions.explanation: Air pollution is associated with increased CO2 and other pollutants, acid rain, and respiratory diseases — not an increase in oxygen release.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the major consequence of global warming?
options: An increase in the overall temperature of the earth's atmosphere.
It provides suitable environment for agricultural development.
It provides us the air (oxygen) we breathe.
It protects us from the harmful effects of the sun's rays.
questions.explanation: Global warming is, by definition, the major consequence of an overall increase in the Earth's atmospheric temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following are best actions to be taken to reduce the emission of carbon dioxide to atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Planting more trees increases CO2 absorption through photosynthesis, helping reduce atmospheric CO2 — unlike expanding industry, more vehicles, or burning more fossil fuels, which increase emissions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In Ethiopia the broad-leafed rain forests are mainly occur in:
questions.explanation: The Kafa zone in southwestern Ethiopia is well known for its broad-leafed rain forests (also the origin of coffee).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the use of forest? It:
questions.explanation: Forests are an important source of medicinal plants, while the other options describe harms caused by deforestation, not uses of forests.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which human activity is the major cause for clearing of forest?
questions.explanation: Clearing land for settlement and harvesting timber for furniture are major human-driven causes of deforestation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is an ex-situ conservation strategy in biodiversity conservation?
questions.explanation: Ex-situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitat, such as in botanical gardens (or zoos/seed banks); national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and biosphere reserves are all in-situ conservation strategies.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the name of the planet found next to Earth?
questions.explanation: This item marks Mars as the planet "next to Earth" in the exam's answer key. (Flagged for teacher verification — Venus is Earth's inner neighbor and Mars its outer neighbor, so depending on the intended direction, either could reasonably be argued; please confirm which the exam intends.)

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following shows the correct sequence of planets when compared to their position in the solar systems?
questions.explanation: Moving outward from the Sun, the correct order of the first four planets is Mercury, Venus, Earth, then Mars.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following sentences is correct about the movement of satellites around the Earth?
options: Geostationary satellites take less time than it takes for the Earth to rotate once on its axis.
Geostationary satellites take more time than it takes for the Earth to rotate once on its axis.
Geostationary satellites move around the Earth independent of the time of rotation of the Earth.
Geostationary satellites take the same time it takes for the Earth to rotate once on its axis.
questions.explanation: By definition, a geostationary satellite orbits in the same time it takes the Earth to rotate once on its axis (about 24 hours), which is why it appears to stay fixed over the same point on Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following sentences is NOT correct about the motion of satellites and planets in the solar system?
options: Planets move around the sun but satellites move around the sun.
Both satellite and planets move at fixed orbit and complete their rotation at a fixed period.
Planets move at fixed orbit but satellites can move at different orbits.
Unlike satellites, planets complete their rotation at a fixed period.
questions.explanation: This statement is incorrect (and self-contradictory as written) because satellites orbit planets, not the sun directly — unlike planets, which do orbit the sun.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The largest planet in our solar system is:
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system by both mass and volume.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: All of the following are the unique characteristics of Earth EXCEPT:
options: it has proper average surface temperature suitable to support life.
it has very thick atmosphere of carbon dioxide.
it is the only planet that has seasons.
it holds the phenomena of forming clouds and rain to get water.
questions.explanation: Earth does not have a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere — that describes Venus. Earth's atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, which is one of the features that makes it uniquely suitable for life.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What makes the Earth to be suitable for life?
options: The existence of large quantities of nitrogen gas in its atmosphere.
The huge size which enable it to hold everything.
The rocky surface and its location from other planets.
The availability of large amount of oxygen and water.
questions.explanation: Earth's rocky surface and its location within the Sun's habitable zone (neither too close nor too far) give it the suitable temperature range and conditions that support life.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the natural source of light?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a natural source of light; candles and oil lamps are artificial sources, and the Moon only reflects sunlight rather than producing its own.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: If white light falls on the front side of a prism, in which order will the colors appear on the other side of the prism?
questions.explanation: White light disperses through a prism into the spectrum in ROYGBIV order: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: The image formed by the concave lens is always:
questions.explanation: A concave (diverging) lens always forms a virtual, upright, and diminished image, regardless of object distance.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the propagation of sound through materials? Sound propagates:
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest through solids, slower through liquids, and slowest through gases, because particles are more tightly packed in solids, allowing faster transmission of vibrations.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: Which one of the following causes of sound pollution is classified under public address system? It is the noise from:
questions.explanation: Noise from loudspeakers used at religious functions is a common example of public address system-related sound pollution.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: If you stand in front of a big wall at some distance and shout, you will hear an echo, this is due to:
questions.explanation: An echo occurs when sound waves reflect off a distant surface (like a wall) and travel back to the listener.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: The form of energy that flows from an object at higher temperature to an object at lower temperature is called--------------
questions.explanation: Heat is the form of energy that flows from a hotter object to a cooler one until thermal equilibrium is reached.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: Which one of the following materials is a good conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Silver, a metal, is an excellent conductor of heat, unlike glass, plastic, and foam, which are good insulators.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: Which one of the following simple circuit components is used as a source of energy?
questions.explanation: A cell (battery) is the component that provides the electrical energy in a simple circuit.

questions.subject: science
questions.chapter: Chapter 6 — Light, Sound, Heat, Electricity & Magnetism
questions.q: If you make an experiment using magnets and certain materials, which of the following expressions could be the result of your experiment?
options: A magnet attracts cobalt, iron and nickel.
A magnet suspended freely on air aligns itself in the east-west direction.
A magnet attracts silver, wood and plastics.
Like poles of magnets attract each other.
questions.explanation: Cobalt, iron, and nickel are the three classic ferromagnetic metals attracted by magnets; a freely suspended magnet aligns north-south (not east-west), non-metals like wood/plastic/silver aren't attracted, and like poles actually repel rather than attract.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In which order does the incoming air pass through the breathing structures of humans?
options: Nasal cavity, Trachea, Bronchi, Nose, Alveoli, Bronchioles
Nasal cavity, Nose, Trachea, Bronchi, Bronchioles, Alveoli
Nose, Nasal cavity, Trachea, Bronchi, Bronchioles, Alveoli
Nasal cavity, Nose, Trachea, Bronchioles, Alveoli, Bronchi
questions.explanation: Air travels: Nose → Nasal cavity → Trachea → Bronchi → Bronchioles → Alveoli, where gas exchange occurs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the main function of human respiratory system? It:
options: transports digested food to the body cells.
supports the body and gives us our distinctive shape.
supplies oxygen to cells and gives out carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: The respiratory system's main function is gas exchange — taking in oxygen for cells and expelling carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Consider the following structures in the human circulatory system: I. Right atrium, II. Pulmonary vein, III. Left ventricle, IV. Pulmonary artery, V. Lungs, VI. Left atrium, VII. Right ventricle. The correct order that shows pulmonary circulation is:
options: I, VI, IV, V, VII, III, II
I, VII, IV, V, II, VI, III
VI, III, IV, V, II, I, VII
I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII
questions.explanation: Pulmonary circulation follows: Right atrium (I) → Right ventricle (VII) → Pulmonary artery (IV) → Lungs (V) → Pulmonary vein (II) → Left atrium (VI); the left ventricle (III) belongs to systemic circulation, not the pulmonary loop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is the main role of the platelets in our blood?
questions.explanation: Platelets are primarily responsible for blood clotting after an injury; transporting oxygen/nutrients is the role of red blood cells and plasma, while defending against pathogens and producing antibodies are roles of white blood cells.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The formation of the great East African rift valley is mainly the result of:
questions.explanation: The East African rift valley formed mainly through faulting — the cracking and displacement of the Earth's crust along fault lines.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: An agent of external force which is common in winter season in Temperate Zone and high mountain areas is:
questions.explanation: Frost action (freeze-thaw weathering) is especially common in cold winters and high mountain areas, where water repeatedly freezes and thaws in rock cracks.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following land form is formed at the lower course of a river?
questions.explanation: Ox bow lakes form in the lower course of a river, where meandering and looping create cut-off curved lakes; V-shaped valleys, waterfalls, and gorges are typically upper/middle course features.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In the stratosphere there is an increasing of temperature with increasing in height, this is because of the concentration of
questions.explanation: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs incoming UV radiation, which causes temperature to increase with height in this layer.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: An atmospheric gas which is present in variable quantities, in the lower atmosphere is
questions.explanation: Unlike nitrogen, oxygen, and argon (which stay relatively constant), water vapor content in the lower atmosphere varies greatly depending on location, temperature, and weather.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT TRUE about the Troposphere?
options: It contains 75% of the total atmospheric masses.
It is the thickest and highest layer of the atmosphere.
It is the denser and lowest layer of the atmosphere.
It contains most of the atmospheric gases.
questions.explanation: The troposphere is actually the lowest and (compared to some other layers) relatively thin layer of the atmosphere — not the thickest and highest, which makes this statement false.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Temperature is the basic elements of weather and climate which is measured by an instrument called:
questions.explanation: Temperature is measured using a thermometer; a barometer measures pressure, a hygrometer measures humidity, and a rain gauge measures rainfall.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which part of Ethiopia gets relatively longer period of rain duration (more than 8 to 10 months)?
questions.explanation: The southwestern highlands of Ethiopia receive a relatively long rainy season, often extending 8 to 10 months of the year.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Marley, Wheat and Pulses are plants which are grown in one of the following climatic zone.
questions.explanation: Barley, wheat, and pulses are cool-climate crops well suited to the dega (highland) climatic zone of Ethiopia.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following language family is largely spoken in China and South East Asia?
questions.explanation: The Sino-Tibetan language family, which includes Chinese and many Southeast/East Asian languages, is largely spoken across China and South East Asia.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following is the major race of Africa, Asia and Pacific islands?
questions.explanation: This item marks Negroid as the major race spanning parts of Africa, South/Southeast Asia, and the Pacific islands in the exam's answer key.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: An ideology that intended to impose Westernization and Americanization over the rest of the world is:
questions.explanation: Globalization is the ideology/process associated with spreading Western and American cultural, economic, and political influence worldwide.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following economic activity provides the direct livelihood at least for half of the world's population?
questions.explanation: Agriculture directly provides the livelihood for at least half of the world's population, particularly in developing countries.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: An economic activity sector which belongs to the provision of services is:
questions.explanation: The tertiary sector of the economy is the one that provides services, distinct from primary (raw material extraction) and secondary (manufacturing) sectors.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The economy of Ethiopia largely depends on:
questions.explanation: Ethiopia's economy has historically depended largely on agriculture, which employs the majority of its population and contributes significantly to GDP and exports.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Trade contributes in the economy of Ethiopia by:
options: increasing competition and lowering world price
questions.explanation: Trade contributes positively to Ethiopia's economy by increasing competition, which can help lower world prices for consumers, unlike the other negatively-framed options.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A type of trade which is concerned with exchange of commodities among people of the same country:
questions.explanation: Domestic trade refers to the exchange of commodities among people within the same country, as opposed to trade across national borders.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following refers to the characteristics of perfectly competitive market?
options: Producers enter and exit the market freely.
The producers are not price takers.
Both buyers and sellers have no perfect information.
questions.explanation: Free entry and exit of producers is a defining characteristic of a perfectly competitive market; in reality, such markets also have homogenous products, price-taking producers, and perfect information — the opposite of options B, C, and D.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following statement describes the government revenue?
options: It is the money received by a government from taxes and non-taxes.
It is taxes initiated by primary industries.
It refers various quantities of commodities produced.
It is levied by the government on their citizens.
questions.explanation: Government revenue is broadly defined as all money a government receives, including both tax and non-tax sources.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In the early time tax in Ethiopia was collected in the form of:
questions.explanation: In early Ethiopian history, taxes were commonly collected "in kind" — as goods or produce — rather than in cash or currency.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Of the following, one is the direct use of natural resources?
options: It is source of energy such as fuel and wood.
It maintains the balance of nature.
questions.explanation: Using natural resources directly as a source of energy (like fuel and wood) is a direct use, while regulating climate, providing aesthetic value, and maintaining nature's balance are indirect ecosystem services.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following factor affects the utilization of natural resources in developing countries?
questions.explanation: Overpopulation places significant pressure on and affects the utilization of natural resources, especially in developing countries.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why the consumption pattern of resources is changing over time? Because:
options: human needs and wants are limited.
people are less dependent on natural resource.
demands on using resources are never ending.
demands on using resources are ending.
questions.explanation: Human demands on resources are never-ending and constantly evolving, which is why consumption patterns keep changing over time.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about resource conservation?
options: It refers the unwise use of natural resources.
It does not contribute to the sustainability of natural resources.
It refers wasteful and destructive way of resource utilization.
It is an act of protecting natural resources.
questions.explanation: Resource conservation is the act of protecting and wisely managing natural resources, the opposite of unwise, wasteful, or destructive use.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A mechanism of soil conservation by covering the soil with plant residue is:
questions.explanation: Mulching is the soil conservation technique that involves covering the soil surface with plant residue or other organic material.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The presence of materials in the air in such concentration which are harmful to man and his environment is:
questions.explanation: Air pollution is defined as the presence of harmful materials/substances in the air at concentrations that damage people and the environment.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following is CORRECT about the relationship between resource and society?
options: Half of world population is directly tied to local natural resources.
Many rural population depends up on manufacturing.
Agriculture is the main source of income for developed countries.
Developed countries are more dependent on natural resources
questions.explanation: About half of the world's population, especially in rural and developing areas, is directly tied to and dependent on local natural resources like land, water, and forests.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The unresolved conflict of interest on the use of Nile River took place among:
questions.explanation: The unresolved conflict over the use of the Nile River's waters (notably over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam) involves Ethiopia, Egypt, and Sudan.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A long term change in the statistical distribution of weather over periods of time is:
questions.explanation: Climate change is defined as a long-term change in the statistical distribution of weather patterns over extended periods of time.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Identify the WRONGLY paired causes of climate change.
options: Emition of carbon dioxide - Human cause
questions.explanation: Volcanic eruptions are a natural cause of climate change, not a human cause — making this the wrongly paired option.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following activity of planting trees practiced in an area where trees have not been grown previously?
questions.explanation: Afforestation is planting trees in an area that had no prior forest cover, distinct from reforestation (replanting where forest existed before).

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the major mechanism practiced by the Konso people to reduce soil erosion?
questions.explanation: The Konso people are famously known (a UNESCO World Heritage site) for their extensive stone terracing to reduce soil erosion on steep slopes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Stop dumping, wastes, in the seas, rivers and lakes are methods of:
questions.explanation: Preventing waste dumping in seas, rivers, and lakes is a method of conserving water resources and protecting water quality.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: The campaign which was announced by the government of Ethiopia to plant trees is known as:
options: The building of The Great Ethiopian Renaissance Dam
questions.explanation: The Green Legacy Initiative is the Ethiopian government's national tree-planting campaign.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: Which of the following explorer circumnavigate the world?
questions.explanation: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition was the first to circumnavigate (sail all the way around) the world.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: One of the following is feature of Renaissance
options: using of Latin language than vernacular in writing
using of religious thinking to advance knowledge
using of reason to improve knowledge
using of ancient Mesopotamian literary works
questions.explanation: The Renaissance was characterized by humanism — the use of reason to improve knowledge — rather than relying purely on religious thinking, and it drew on ancient Greek and Roman (not Mesopotamian) works, alongside a rise in vernacular writing.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: Which one of the following is characterized Reformation?
questions.explanation: The Reformation is characterized by the split of Protestantism from the Catholic Church, led by figures like Martin Luther, not Renaissance artists like Michelangelo or Leonardo da Vinci.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: Industrial Revolution characterized by
options: using of simple hand tools than machines.
changes source of energy and knowledge of production.
began in Italy in 18th C and spread to the rest of the world.
was ongoing revolution using the old technology.
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution was characterized by major changes in energy sources (like steam power) and production knowledge/technology — it began in Britain, not Italy, and shifted away from simple hand tools.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: Which one of the following is result of Industrial Revolution?
options: Emergence of two new social classes.
Creates working opportunity and reduced unemployment.
Working class able to lead better life.
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution led to the emergence of two new major social classes: the industrial bourgeoisie (factory owners) and the working class (proletariat).

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: Among the following one was NOT the basic cause of WWI.
options: Killing of Austrian prince Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo.
questions.explanation: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand was the immediate trigger/spark of WWI, not one of its underlying basic causes, which included alliances, militarism, and colonial rivalries.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: During WWI, the Germany Schlieffen war plan was targeted.
options: to attack Russia and Austro-Hungary at once
to attack the German force from two fronts
to avoid German forces fighting on two fronts at once
to attract German enemies to fight at several fronts
questions.explanation: The Schlieffen Plan aimed to quickly defeat France in the west before Russia could fully mobilize in the east, avoiding a prolonged two-front war for Germany.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: Which of the following is resulted after the end of WWI?
options: Formation of the United Nations Organization.
The division of the world in two camps of west and east.
Decolonization of Africa and Asian states.
Formation of the League of Nations.
questions.explanation: The League of Nations was formed after the end of WWI (1920); the United Nations, Cold War division, and decolonization all came later, after WWII.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: An international organization founded following the end of WWII.
questions.explanation: The United Nations was founded in 1945, immediately following the end of World War II.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: During Cold War the western bloc was composed of
questions.explanation: The western bloc during the Cold War was composed of the USA and its allies, including Britain and France; the USSR and China belonged to (or aligned closer with) the eastern/communist bloc.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: Why anti-slavery movement began and expanded? Because
questions.explanation: The anti-slavery movement grew largely due to moral and humanitarian opposition to the harsh, exploitative nature of the slave trade.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 4 — World History: Renaissance to World Wars
questions.q: What was the role of Abolitionist movement in slavery and slave trade?
options: Aimed to stop slavery as illegal trade.
Forced slaves to stand for their rights.
Aimed to make slavery as legal trade.
questions.explanation: The Abolitionist movement's role was to campaign to end slavery, working to have it declared and treated as an illegal trade.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE about the scramble for Africa?
options: European controlled the whole Africa at about 1870.
Africans were controlled by Britain and France only.
By 1895, 90 percent of Africa was under European control.
African countries were involved in the scrambling
questions.explanation: By 1895, approximately 90 percent of Africa had come under European colonial control, a widely cited fact about the scramble for Africa.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why African resistance against colonial expansion failed? Because
options: Africans had no unity among themselves.
Early resistance of Africans was better organized.
questions.explanation: A major reason African resistance often failed was the lack of unity among different African groups and kingdoms, which colonial powers could exploit.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: African independence movement was successful after WWII, because
options: colonial powers lost interest on their colonies
USA and USSR supported colonial forces
Africans got useful military experience on the war.
questions.explanation: Many Africans served as soldiers in WWII and gained valuable military experience and exposure to ideas of self-determination, which fueled post-war independence movements.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why Africans founded the OAU after liberation?
options: To make Africans to be industrialized
Work together for colonialism to be continued
To end all forms of colonialism from Africa.
questions.explanation: A core founding purpose of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) was to work together to end all remaining forms of colonialism across Africa.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The OAU was succeeded in one of the following in its history
options: in advancing economic growth of Africans
in preventing civil war within Africa
questions.explanation: The OAU is widely credited with supporting and helping bring about the end of colonialism across Africa, even though it struggled in other areas like preventing civil wars.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A king aimed to unify the country by ending Zemene Mesafint?
questions.explanation: Emperor Tewodros II is credited with ending the Zemene Mesafint ("Era of the Princes") and beginning the modern unification of Ethiopia.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which policy of Yohannis IV applied in his state formation process?
options: He made Tewahido to be official religion.
He made Catholicism to be official religion.
He made Islam to be official religion.
He made Protestantism to be official religion.
questions.explanation: Emperor Yohannis IV declared Orthodox Tewahido Christianity as the official state religion as part of his state formation policy.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: One of the following successfully took several actions in modernize the state
questions.explanation: Emperor Menilik II is widely credited with taking successful modernizing actions, including introducing infrastructure, schools, and new institutions to the Ethiopian state.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Muslim traders of long distance across Shawa, Harar towards northern Somalia were
questions.explanation: This item marks Arggoba as the term for these long-distance Muslim traders in the exam's answer key. (Flagged for teacher verification, since the historical terms for long-distance Muslim traders and trade administrators in this region can be easily confused — please double check this item against the source material.)

questions.subject: social
questions.q: European missionary who facilitated Italian occupation of Assab was
questions.explanation: Giuseppe Sapeto, an Italian missionary, negotiated the purchase of the port of Assab that facilitated Italy's occupation there in 1869.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following British travellers came to Ethiopia in 1840s?
questions.explanation: John Bell and Walter Plowden were British travelers/advisors who came to Ethiopia in the 1840s and became closely involved with Emperor Tewodros II's court.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: One of the following battles Ethiopians fought differed from the others
questions.explanation: The Battle of Adwa (1896), fought against Italy and resulting in internationally recognized Ethiopian independence, is distinguished from the other battles listed.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: One of the following treaty finally led Yohannis IV to fight against Mahidist Forces
questions.explanation: The Hewett Treaty (1884) committed Emperor Yohannis IV to assist the evacuation of Egyptian garrisons from Sudan, drawing him into conflict with the Mahdist forces.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Ethiopian patriotic resistance against Fascist rule in 1941 was supported by
questions.explanation: Britain supported the Ethiopian patriotic resistance during the 1941 East African Campaign that helped liberate Ethiopia from Fascist Italian occupation.

questions.explanation: (-5/9)³ = -125/729 (negative, since a negative number cubed stays negative).
