questions.subject: science
questions.q: A homologous series is any two consecutive members of organic compounds that have the same functional groups but differ in:
questions.explanation: Consecutive members of a homologous series differ by one CH₂ group. They share the same general formula and similar chemical properties. NOTE: teacher to verify.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sulfur dioxide is produced in the laboratory by burning elemental sulfur in oxygen according to the following reaction: S + O₂ → SO₂. When it starts burning, SO₂ is collected a gas jar and small amount of water is added to it. Finally, blue and red litmus papers are put one after the other in the jar containing the solution. What happens to the colors of the litmus papers?
options: Blue litmus paper changes its color into red.
Both litmus papers change their color.
Red litmus paper changes its color into blue.
The solution has no effect on both litmus papers.
questions.explanation: SO₂ dissolves in water to form sulfurous acid. Acids turn blue litmus red and leave red litmus unchanged.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a certain experiment, a teacher wanted to demonstrate the effect of calcium hydroxide on litmus paper. The teacher took a portion of calcium hydroxide solution in a test tube and put litmus paper in it. Which one of the following observation would you think is CORRECT? Calcium hydroxide:
options: turns blue litmus paper into red.
has no effect on red litmus paper.
turns red litmus paper into blue.
has no effect on litmus paper.
questions.explanation: Calcium hydroxide is a base. Bases turn red litmus paper blue and do not change blue litmus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of alkane, alkene and alkyne with seven carbon atoms respectively?
questions.explanation: Alkane CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ = C₇H₁₆; alkene CₙH₂ₙ = C₇H₁₄; alkyne CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ = C₇H₁₂.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The structure of integumentary system which occurs in all over the body except the palm and sole, and secretes an oily semifluid to lubricate our skin is:
questions.explanation: Sebaceous (oil) glands are found all over the skin except the palms and soles and secrete oily sebum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is an inherited muscle disorder characterized by muscle weakness and a loss of muscle tissue?
questions.explanation: Muscular dystrophy is a group of inherited disorders causing progressive muscle weakness and loss of muscle tissue.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the main function of human skeletal system?
options: Absorbing of digested nutrients to body cells.
Making new blood cells within the narrow cavities.
questions.explanation: Bone marrow inside the bone cavities makes new blood cells; this is a main function of the skeleton.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which structure of the digestive system and its description is CORRECT?
options: Small intestine: is divided into cecum, colon, and rectum.
Large intestine: is the tube that extends from the pharynx to stomach.
Mouth: is the beginning of the digestive tube where food is taken in.
Stomach: is divided into duodenum, jejunum and ileum.
questions.explanation: The mouth is where food enters the digestive tube. The small intestine has duodenum, jejunum and ileum; the large intestine has cecum, colon and rectum; the oesophagus links the pharynx to the stomach. NOTE: the pencil mark in the photo pointed to another option; teacher to verify.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Respiratory disorder which is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria is known as ______.
questions.explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis causes tuberculosis (TB) of the lungs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is CORRECT about the structure and function of mammalian heart?
options: Left auricle – receives oxygenated blood from lungs.
Left ventricle – pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
Right auricle – receives oxygenated blood from lungs.
Right ventricle – pumps oxygenated blood to the body.
questions.explanation: The left auricle (atrium) receives oxygenated blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the primary sexual characteristic in males?
options: Presence of penis, testes, and scrotum.
Production of sperm cells and sex hormones.
Broadening and widening of chest and shoulder.
questions.explanation: Primary sexual characteristics are the reproductive organs present from birth (penis, testes, scrotum). Voice deepening and chest broadening are secondary characteristics. NOTE: teacher to verify.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In biological relationship of commensalism:
options: one organism is benefited and the other is neutral.
one organism is benefited and the other is harmed.
neither of the organisms is benefited.
questions.explanation: In commensalism one organism benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed. (Harm to the other is parasitism; both benefiting is mutualism.)

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The exchange of necessary nutrients between living organisms and non-living world is very important because nutrients are:
questions.explanation: Nutrients are limited in nature, so they must be recycled continuously between living things and the environment.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following methods is used to conserve soil?
options: Planting the same crop year after year.
Cutting down forest trees for fuel and construction.
Planting trees on a land which is affected by deforestation.
Burning materials left in an agricultural field after the crop has been harvested.
questions.explanation: Planting trees on degraded land (afforestation) holds the soil and prevents erosion. Cutting trees and burning residue harm the soil. NOTE: the pencil mark in the photo pointed to another option; teacher to verify.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In nature water provides all the following functions, EXCEPT:
options: producing food in plants by photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Water helps regulate body temperature, drives hydroelectric turbines and is a raw material of photosynthesis, but it does not develop the electronics industry.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is the major consequence of global warming?
options: An increase in the overall temperature of the earth's atmosphere.
Providing suitable environment for agricultural development.
Providing us the air (oxygen) we breathe.
Protecting us from the harmful effects of the sun's rays.
questions.explanation: Global warming is the rise in the overall temperature of the earth's atmosphere.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following actions must be taken to conserve forests?
options: Establishing private and public forest reserves.
Cutting down forest trees for fuel and construction.
Cutting of young trees only and protection of mature trees.
questions.explanation: Establishing protected forest reserves conserves forests; the other options damage them.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following given orders shows the CORRECT order of planets in the solar system from the sun?
questions.explanation: From the Sun the order is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. NOTE: the pencil mark in the photo pointed to another option.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE about the motion of all planets in the solar systems? All planets:
options: move in orbital motion are in the ant clock wise direction.
move around the sun in the same direction that of the sun rotates.
move around the sun in opposite direction that of the sun rotates.
orbit around the sun in the anti-clock wise path called elliptical path.
questions.explanation: All planets revolve around the Sun in the same direction as the Sun's own rotation. NOTE: options A and D are also commonly stated in textbooks (anti-clockwise, elliptical orbits) and the photo's pencil mark pointed to D — teacher to verify against the official key.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of the following is TRUE about the position and characteristics of Planets from the Sun?
options: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and hotter than Venus.
Earth is the second closest planet to the Sun and hotter than Mercury.
Venus is the second closest planet to the Sun and hotter than Mercury.
Mars is the second closest planet to the Sun and is hotter than Mercury.
questions.explanation: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and, because of its thick greenhouse atmosphere, is hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is closer.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What makes our Earth different from any other planets? Our Earth:
options: has a temperature just not for life.
has a small amount of oxygen in its atmosphere.
It is the only planet known to support life.
questions.explanation: Earth is the only planet known to support life.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which one of following characteristics represents the reflection of light? Reflection is:
options: the splitting of white light in to different colors.
getting bent when light travels obliquely from one transparent material to another.
the bending of white light back when it strikes the surface of a body.
passing directly from one transparent material into another transparent material.
questions.explanation: Reflection is light bouncing back when it strikes a surface. Splitting is dispersion; bending on entering another material is refraction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Of the following, one is the nature of an image formed by a convex mirror.
options: The image is same size of as the size of the object.
The image is smaller than the size of the object.
The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of the mirror.
Left and right sides of the object appear to change on the image in the mirror.
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, upright, diminished (smaller) image. Options C and D describe a plane mirror. NOTE: the pencil mark in the photo pointed to another option; teacher to verify.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sound can NOT travel through:
questions.explanation: Sound needs a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel; it cannot pass through a vacuum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Consider the following materials: I. Copper  II. Silver  III. Iron  IV. Rubber  V. Glass  VI. Plastic. Which one of the following sets of materials is a good conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Metals (copper, silver, iron) are good conductors of heat; rubber, glass and plastic are insulators.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is CORRECT about magnetic lines of force? Magnetic lines of force:
options: run from North Pole to South Pole inside a magnet.
run from South Pole to North Pole outside a magnet.
run from South Pole to North Pole inside a magnet.
originate from North Pole and end on South Pole of a magnet.
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines run from the North to the South pole outside a magnet and return from South to North inside it (they form closed loops). NOTE: option D is also a common textbook wording for the outside field — teacher to verify.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: According to some scientists' belief, the earth was mostly formed from one of the following pair of elements.
questions.explanation: Scientists' theories of Earth's formation say the early solar nebula was made mostly of hydrogen and helium gases.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is the characteristic of major earth forming minerals?
options: They have definite physical state and chemical composition.
All are formed in combination with other minerals.
They do not have definite crystalline structure.
questions.explanation: Minerals are naturally occurring, inorganic solids with a definite chemical composition and crystalline structure.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which types of sedimentary rock is formed from the decomposition of plants and animals' remain?
questions.explanation: Organic sedimentary rocks (e.g. coal, some limestone) form from the accumulation and decay of plant and animal remains.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: According to the scientists, which part of the world is considered to be the cradle of human beings?
questions.explanation: Earliest human fossils (e.g. Lucy, Ardi) were found in the East African Rift Valley, so it is called the cradle of humankind.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following region is the most populous in the world?
questions.explanation: East Asia (China, Japan, Korea) is among the most densely populated regions; the Sahara and Tundra are sparsely populated.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The marine boat transportation system was invented for the first time by:
questions.explanation: Ancient Egyptians are credited with the earliest boats and sailing ships on the Nile and Red Sea. (Note: please have a teacher verify this answer — the pencil mark in the photographed paper differed or the wording is ambiguous.)

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Of the following modes of transport, which one is the cheapest and suitable for transporting bulky goods over long distance?
questions.explanation: Water transport (ships) carries very heavy, bulky goods over long distances at the lowest cost per unit.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following can be an advisable road safety rule for all drivers?
questions.explanation: Never drink and drive is the only safe rule; the other options describe dangerous behavior.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true about the relationship between human beings and their environment?
options: There is one way relationship between them.
Environment can influence human beings life style.
Human beings can influence their environment.
Science and technology can help us to use the environment.
questions.explanation: The relationship is two-way: environment influences people and people influence the environment.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Over population scenario in human and environment relationship occurs when:
options: available resources are greater than country's population needs.
available resources are equal to country's population needs.
there is optimal utilization of resource and infrastructure.
available resources are less than the country's population needs.
questions.explanation: Overpopulation means the population is too large for the available resources to meet its needs.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In what way does a renewable resources are different from the non-renewable resources?
options: They are minerals like, Diamond and Gold.
They are available in infinite quantity.
questions.explanation: Renewable resources (sun, wind, water) are practically unlimited or replenish quickly; the other options describe non-renewables. (Note: please have a teacher verify this answer — the pencil mark in the photographed paper differed or the wording is ambiguous.)

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is the major human cause that affect natural environment in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Deforestation (cutting forests for farmland, fuel wood) is the major human-caused environmental problem in Ethiopia.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which set of rivers is correctly paired with the ancient civilization that developed along its banks?
questions.explanation: Nile–Egypt, Tigris & Euphrates–Mesopotamia, Indus–India, Yellow River–China.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which writing system is associated with Egyptian civilization?
questions.explanation: Egyptians wrote with hieroglyphics; cuneiform is Mesopotamian, Sanskrit is Indian, bone script is Chinese.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What was the primary reason the Quarysh tribe opposed Prophet Mohammed's teaching?
options: He attacks on idolatry threatened their income.
They wanted to convert to Judaism instead of Islam.
They disagreed with his marriage to a wealthy wisdom.
They believed, he was a political threat to their alliance with Persia.
questions.explanation: The Quraysh earned wealth from pilgrims visiting idols at the Kaaba, so attacks on idolatry threatened their income.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What was the main reason that the Roman government initially began to persecute Christians?
options: Christians were trying to overthrow the emperor
Christians refused to worship the state gods and Emperors.
Christians were stealing property from the Roman citizens's.
questions.explanation: Christians refused to worship Roman gods and the emperor, which Rome saw as disloyalty.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What was the name of the most impressive Christian Church built in Constantinople under Emperor Justinian I?
questions.explanation: Hagia Sophia was built under Justinian I in the 6th century.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following was the contribution of ancient Egypt?
options: Controlled the trade along the India Oceans.
questions.explanation: Ancient Egyptians developed the first 365-day solar calendar.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Nubians lived in Northern Nile valley between
questions.explanation: Nubia stretched along the Nile from Aswan (Egypt) to Dongola (Sudan).

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following was the cause for the decline of the kingdom of Meroe?
options: The occupation of the Red sea.
The rise of rival Aksum Kingdom.
The rise of Islam in the region.
questions.explanation: Aksum's rise and its attack on Meroe (c. 350 AD) ended the kingdom; Islam came centuries later. (Note: please have a teacher verify this answer — the pencil mark in the photographed paper differed or the wording is ambiguous.)

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 5 — African & Ethiopian History (Ancient to Medieval)
questions.q: Which factor mainly contributed to the growth of ancient Ghana and Songhai Empire?
questions.explanation: Both empires grew rich by controlling the Trans-Saharan trade in gold and salt.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 5 — African & Ethiopian History (Ancient to Medieval)
questions.q: What was the importance of king Ezana in the history of Aksum?
questions.explanation: King Ezana adopted Christianity (c. 330 AD) and made it the state religion of Aksum.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 5 — African & Ethiopian History (Ancient to Medieval)
questions.q: Why did Gondar become important city in Ethiopian history? Because
options: it became the center of culture and architecture.
questions.explanation: Gondar, founded by Emperor Fasiledes, became a center of culture, art and castle architecture.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 5 — African & Ethiopian History (Ancient to Medieval)
questions.q: Which one of the following was the main source of conflict between the sultanate of Ifat and the Christian Highland Kingdom in the medieval period?
options: Sultanate of Ifat refused to pay annual tribute
To control the Zeila trade and trade routes
The Christian highland kingdom was refused to pay tribute.
To control the pastoral land of the northern part of the regions
questions.explanation: Both sides wanted control of the Zeila trade outlet and the trade routes to the coast.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 5 — African & Ethiopian History (Ancient to Medieval)
questions.q: Which of the following was the reason for the Oromo population movement and expansion?
options: The high interaction between Oromo and the Christian highland kingdom.
Population growth and substantial increase of their cattle.
The intervention of the external powers for support.
The adoption of the Barentu and Borena confederacies.
questions.explanation: Rapid population growth and cattle increase created need for new pasture, causing expansion.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Of the following methods protecting the environment, which one gives proper knowledge on ecosystem and sustainability?
questions.explanation: Environmental education teaches people about ecosystems and sustainable use.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Deforestation, rapid population growth and depletion of resources are the major environmental problems of mostly:
questions.explanation: These problems are most severe in developing countries.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why Terrorism can slow economic development of the world? Because it:
questions.explanation: Terrorism destroys infrastructure, scares away investment and tourism, and disrupts trade.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following land forms are created by internal forces?
questions.explanation: Mountains and rift valleys are formed by internal (tectonic) forces; the others are formed by external forces (water, wind).

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The common agents of external weathering in temperate zone and in some high mountain areas are:
questions.explanation: Frost action (freeze–thaw) is the common weathering agent in cold temperate and high mountain areas.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following gas is concentrated in the same proportion in the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Argon stays at a constant proportion; water vapor and CO₂ vary by place and time.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A seasonal wind which is very common in South and Southeast Asia is:
questions.explanation: Monsoon winds reverse seasonally and dominate South and Southeast Asia.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the followings best describes the temperature and rainfall characteristics of highland and lowland areas?
options: Highlands experience hot temperature and low rainfall.
Lowlands experience cooler temperature and they are wet.
Highlands experience low temperature and high rainfall.
questions.explanation: Highlands are cooler and receive more rainfall than lowlands.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A language which is widely spoken in China and several smaller countries in South East Asia is:
questions.explanation: Chinese belongs to the Sino-Tibetan language family.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: An economic activity which provides the direct livelihood for about half of the world's population is:
questions.explanation: Agriculture supports roughly half of the world's population.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT true about the economy of developed countries?
options: It is mainly based on agriculture.
It is mainly urban based economy.
It is specialized in commercial activities.
It is supported by sophisticated technology.
questions.explanation: Developed economies rely mainly on industry and services, not agriculture.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Ethiopia exports coffee to other countries and earns foreign currency. What does this show about the rule of trade?
options: Trade decreases the Ethiopian national income
Trade helps Ethiopia to earn hard currency
Trade limits economic growth of Ethiopia
questions.explanation: Exports bring in foreign (hard) currency.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following conditions exist when perfect competition to occur?
options: All producers contribute significantly to the market
questions.explanation: In perfect competition producers can enter and leave the market freely (products are homogeneous, no single producer dominates). (Note: please have a teacher verify this answer — the pencil mark in the photographed paper differed or the wording is ambiguous.)

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A compulsory financial charge or some other type of levy imposed on a tax payer by government institution is?
questions.explanation: A tax is a compulsory financial charge imposed by government.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In the earlier time people mainly depend on which resource for energy?
questions.explanation: Early people relied on wood (fire) and animal/human power.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A mechanism of soil conservation, that practiced by covering the soil with plant residues is?
questions.explanation: Mulching covers the soil with plant residues to reduce erosion and keep moisture.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The presence of materials in the air in such constriction (concentration) which are harmful to human beings and their environments is:
questions.explanation: Harmful materials in the air at high concentration are called air pollution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: If communities cooperate in managing common resource, what is the likely result?
questions.explanation: Cooperation leads to better management and sustainable use.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 10 — World History: Exploration to the Cold War
questions.q: Imagine you are an explorer in the 16th century. Your goal is to be the first to sail around the world. Based on this, whose route would you try to follow?
questions.explanation: Magellan's expedition (1519–1522) was the first to circumnavigate the globe.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 10 — World History: Exploration to the Cold War
questions.q: What was Martin Luther's primary opposition to the Catholic Church that started the Reformation?
options: The use of Latin in Church Services.
The church wealth and political power.
The authority of the Pope over church
The church practice of selling properties.
questions.explanation: Luther's 95 Theses attacked the Church's sale of indulgences (the option says 'selling properties'). (Note: please have a teacher verify this answer — the pencil mark in the photographed paper differed or the wording is ambiguous.)

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 10 — World History: Exploration to the Cold War
questions.q: What was the most significant change that characterized the first phase of industrial revolution?
options: The change from using coal to petroleum.
The change from using iron to using steel.
The change from machine to manual labor.
The change from manual labor to machine labor.
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution replaced manual labor with machine labor.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 10 — World History: Exploration to the Cold War
questions.q: If you were asked to create a better military plan, the Schlieffen plan, what should be your first priority?
options: Avoid fighting on the two fronts at the same time
questions.explanation: The Schlieffen plan was designed to avoid a two-front war for Germany (France and Russia).

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 10 — World History: Exploration to the Cold War
questions.q: Which of the following was the main feature of the cold war?
questions.explanation: The Cold War was mainly an ideological struggle between capitalism (USA) and communism (USSR). (Note: please have a teacher verify this answer — the pencil mark in the photographed paper differed or the wording is ambiguous.)

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 11 — Slave Trade, Colonialism & Ethiopian Resistance
questions.q: The historians arguing that economic factors were the primary drivers for the end of the slave trade, which was the evidence for this?
options: The establishment of Freetown a settlement for freed slave.
The abolitionist movement, which began in Britain.
The Jamaican revolts that liberate colony from slavery.
The shift of machine labor made slavery less important.
questions.explanation: The economic argument: industrial machines made slave labor less profitable.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 11 — Slave Trade, Colonialism & Ethiopian Resistance
questions.q: If an African leader wanted to successfully resist European colonization like Ethiopia, which strategy would be the most important to follow?
options: Form an alliance with other European powers
Maintain unity and organize strong military resistance.
Rely on traditional weapons and spiritual protections
questions.explanation: Ethiopia won at Adwa (1896) through national unity and organized modern military resistance.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 11 — Slave Trade, Colonialism & Ethiopian Resistance
questions.q: What was the main difference between Casablanca and Monrovian group?
options: The former supported colonization, while the later opposed it.
The former against independence, while the later supported it.
The former was formed by Francophone, while the later was by Anglophone.
The former wanted rapid political union while the later a loose association.
questions.explanation: Casablanca group wanted rapid political union; Monrovia group preferred gradual, loose cooperation.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 11 — Slave Trade, Colonialism & Ethiopian Resistance
questions.q: Which one of the following is true about the reforms of Emperor Tewodros II?
options: Reunification was denounced by the peasants.
Gafat became a central place for the manufacturing cannon.
questions.explanation: Tewodros II made Gafat a center for making cannon (including 'Sebastopol'); he abolished the slave trade and centralized power.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 11 — Slave Trade, Colonialism & Ethiopian Resistance
questions.q: Which countries became the major threats for Ethiopian sovereignty during the reign of Emperor Yohannis (IV)?
questions.explanation: Yohannis IV faced Egypt, the Mahdist Sudan and Italy. (Note: please have a teacher verify this answer — the pencil mark in the photographed paper differed or the wording is ambiguous.)

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 11 — Slave Trade, Colonialism & Ethiopian Resistance
questions.q: Which one of the following was the active market center along the long-distance trade route that advanced from Bonga to Zeila via Harar?
questions.explanation: Assendabo (Gibe region) was a major market center on the Bonga–Harar–Zeila caravan route. (Note: please have a teacher verify this answer — the pencil mark in the photographed paper differed or the wording is ambiguous.)

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 11 — Slave Trade, Colonialism & Ethiopian Resistance
questions.q: What was the main focus of the treaties signed in the first half of the 19th century between Ethiopian regional rulers and European representatives?
questions.explanation: Early 19th-century treaties (e.g. Anglo-Ethiopian 1841) focused mainly on trade.

questions.subject: social
questions.chapter: Chapter 11 — Slave Trade, Colonialism & Ethiopian Resistance
questions.q: Which one of the following personalities made collaboration with Italians, when many Ethiopians paid sacrifices for the sovereignty of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Answer not confirmed: all four options are commonly remembered as patriots. The photographed pencil mark was on option B, but this needs teacher review before setting the answer.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which human activity can be a cause for climatic change?
questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases that drive climate change.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which one of the following is a major problem caused by water shortage?
questions.explanation: Water shortage means people lack clean drinking water.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the responsibility of a community in protecting their environment?
questions.explanation: Communities protect the environment by organizing tree planting and similar activities.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: (For non-blind students) If a number of live births in a population of 20,000,000 were 40,000, what is the crude birth rate of the area?

questions.subject: social
questions.q: (For blind students only) Which of the following is a result of rapid population growth?
questions.explanation: Rapid population growth increases pressure on resources and leads to environmental degradation.

questions.q: Konni woroonni noo wo'ma kiiro giddonni 6 kiirora gatiweelo beehantannoti hiittenneeti? (Which number is divisible by 6?)
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 6 if it is even and its digit sum is divisible by 3. 4026 is even and 4+0+2+6 = 12, so it is divisible by 6.

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Mittu daddalaanchi 12,500 birrinni hidhino gerecho 1,000 birra tirfi're bi'rizo tirfesi xibbikkihuuni mageeshshaati? (Profit percent: cost 12,500 birr, profit 1,000 birr)
questions.explanation: Profit % = 1,000 ÷ 12,500 × 100 = 8%. (Note: the question wording is in Sidaamu and was read from a blurry photo; a Sidaamu-speaking teacher should confirm the answer.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: y nna w galchammete beehanchinrna xaadooshshe afidhinota ikkituro aante noori giddo gara ikkinohu hiikkonneeti? (If y and w are inversely proportional, which statement is true?)
options: y nna w duucha woyte taalo ikkitanno.
y waagi lexxanno woyte w waagi xeanno.
y waagi xeanno woyte w waagino xeanno.
y waagi lexxanno woyte w waagino lexxanno.
questions.explanation: In inverse proportion, when one quantity increases the other decreases. Options C and D describe both changing in the same direction (direct proportion). (Note: the question wording is in Sidaamu and was read from a blurry photo; a Sidaamu-speaking teacher should confirm the answer.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Shallagaamu handaari 3x − 4y + 5z + 6 giddo me''u taqi afamanno? (How many terms?)
questions.explanation: The terms are 3x, −4y, 5z and 6, so there are 4 terms.

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Taalleenyu coyfooliishsho 2x + 5 = 31 adda assanno x waagi me''eho?

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Aane noo doorshi giddo 2x − 3 ≥ 5 ledo taalcho ikkitino taalimaweelo coyfooliishsho hiikkonneeti? (Which inequality has the same solution as 2x − 3 ≥ 5?)
questions.explanation: 2x − 3 ≥ 5 → 2x ≥ 8 → x ≥ 4. (Note: some option text in this question was hard to read in the photo — please compare with the printed paper.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Konni woroonni noo angilla giddo obitusse angile ikkitinoti hiittenneeti? (Which angle is obtuse?)
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is greater than 90° and less than 180°. 179° is obtuse; 191° is reflex, 90° is right and 55° is acute.

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Aante noo misilera l nna m lame mimmito tayisse sa'anno xuruurraati. Misilete garinni waaxo gurcho angilla ikkinohu hiikkonneeti? (Which pair are vertically opposite angles?)
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles lie across from each other at the crossing point. In the figure r is opposite t, and s is opposite u, so ∠u and ∠s are the opposite pair. The angle positions were read from the photographed figure. (Note: the question wording is in Sidaamu and was read from a blurry photo; a Sidaamu-speaking teacher should confirm the answer.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Konni woroonni noori giddo rekitaangilete akata ikkinohu hiikkonneeti? (Which is a property of a rectangle?)
questions.explanation: In a rectangle the opposite sides are equal. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal (not different), and the interior angles add up to 360°, not 180°. This is a best reading of the Sidaamu wording. (Note: the question wording is in Sidaamu and was read from a blurry photo; a Sidaamu-speaking teacher should confirm the answer.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Aante shiqqino misile mitte shoode akooda taaraddu xuruurra l, m, n nna k tayisse sa'ino misile leellishshanno. Tayisse sa'ino xuruurra l, m, n nna k giddo biikku suwashsho taashshe beehanno xuruurraati? (Which line is the line of symmetry of the arrow?)
questions.explanation: The arrow is symmetric about the horizontal line through the middle of its shaft and head (k): the parts above and below it are mirror images. The vertical lines l and m and the slanted line n cut it into unequal parts. Line positions were read from the blurry photographed figure. (Note: some option text in this question was hard to read in the photo — please compare with the printed paper.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Uduunne worranni saaxine seendille 3m, godowa 5m nna hojja 4m ikkituro amadose m³ nni me''e ikkitanno? (Volume of a box 3 m × 5 m × 4 m)
questions.explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 3 × 5 × 4 = 60 m³.

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Aante noori giddo shooli midaadaame piriizime akata ikkinokkihu hiikkonneeti?
questions.explanation: Answer not confirmed — the Sidaamu wording (a property of a prism that is NOT true) could not be read reliably. (Note: the question wording is in Sidaamu and was read from a blurry photo; a Sidaamu-speaking teacher should confirm the answer.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Sasi-midaadu piiraamidera xaphoomu albuwate batinyi me''eho? (Number of faces of a triangular pyramid)
questions.explanation: A triangular pyramid has 1 triangular base and 3 triangular side faces, so 4 faces in total. (If the question was about edges the answer would be 6.) (Note: the question wording is in Sidaamu and was read from a blurry photo; a Sidaamu-speaking teacher should confirm the answer.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Aante nooti pokki 75, 48, 97, 64, 20, 17, 56 nna 83 miidiyaane ikkinohu hiikkonneeti? (Median of 75, 48, 97, 64, 20, 17, 56, 83)
questions.explanation: Order the numbers: 17, 20, 48, 56, 64, 75, 83, 97. With 8 values the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: (56 + 64) ÷ 2 = 60. (Note: some option text in this question was hard to read in the photo — please compare with the printed paper.)

questions.subject: shallaggo
questions.q: Aante shiqqino misile nooti maateta aganu fulo xaphooma 18,000 birra piy-chartetinni suwashshi. Chaartete garinni aante shiqqinori giddo adda ikkinohu hiikkonneeti? (Pie chart of a family's monthly expenses, total 18,000 birr — which statement is correct?)
questions.explanation: The Rosu sector is 100° of 360°: 100/360 × 18,000 = 5,000 birr, so B is correct. (The Caabbicho sector of 35° gives 1,750 birr, not 1,500.) Reading passage — "Layinki Niwaawe" (transcribed from blurry photos; […] marks words that could not be read):

Donu mitte dagara ayimmate xawishshaati. Qoleno, […] miinju bueeti. Donu mitte dagata […] yanna manchi beettita kalaqate dandoosi horoonsi're […] leellishanno egenno xawisanno. […] donu ba''annokki gede assa hasiissanno qoropho […] shiqqanno.

Kinsannikki donu dana duachu garinni xawisa dandinanni. […]

Kinsannihano ikko kinsannikki doni dagoomaho babbaxxino horo aanno. Insano, ayyaanaamitie horo, dhaggete horo, ogimmate horo, miinja horo, poletikunna budu horo yinannireeti.

questions.subject: maths
questions.q: ሁለት ትይዩ መስመሮች በአንድ ቀጥታ መስመር ሲቆረጡ ከሚከተሉት ውስጥ ትክክለኛ የሆነው የቱ ነው?
questions.explanation: ትይዩ መስመሮች በአንድ ቀጥታ መስመር ሲቆረጡ ∠1 እና ∠5 በተመሳሳይ አቅጣጫ ስለሚገኙ ተጓዳኝ (corresponding) አንግሎች ናቸው። (ማስታወሻ፦ ይህ ጥያቄ ከተበላሸ ቅጂ በአዲስ መልክ ተጽፏል፤ ምስሉ ስላልተካተተ መምህር ከወረቀቱ ጋር ያመሳክረው።)

questions.subject: maths
questions.q: ሁለት ትይዩ መስመሮች በአንድ ቀጥታ መስመር ሲቆረጡ የ∠3 መጠን 120° ቢሆን የ∠5 መጠን ስንት ይሆናል?
questions.explanation: ∠3 እና ∠5 ተከታታይ ውስጣዊ አንግሎች ናቸው፤ ድምራቸው 180° ነው። ስለዚህ ∠5 = 180° − 120° = 60°። (ማስታወሻ፦ ይህ ጥያቄ ከተበላሸ ቅጂ በአዲስ መልክ ተጽፏል፤ ምስሉ ስላልተካተተ መምህር ከወረቀቱ ጋር ያመሳክረው።)

questions.subject: maths
questions.q: ከሚከተሉት የርዝመት ስብስቦች ውስጥ የሦስት ማዕዘን ጎኖች ሊሆኑ የሚችሉት የትኞቹ ናቸው?
questions.explanation: የሁለት ጎኖች ድምር ከሦስተኛው ጎን መብለጥ አለበት። ሀ፦ 1+2=3 ✗፣ ለ፦ 2+3=5>4 ✓፣ ሐ፦ 2+3=5 ✗፣ መ፦ 5+5=10 ✗። (ማስታወሻ፦ ይህ ጥያቄ ከተበላሸ ቅጂ በአዲስ መልክ ተጽፏል፤ ምስሉ ስላልተካተተ መምህር ከወረቀቱ ጋር ያመሳክረው።)

questions.subject: maths
questions.q: ከሚከተሉት ቅርጾች ውስጥ አራቱም ማዕዘኖቹ ትክክለኛ ማዕዘን (90°) የሆኑት የትኛው ነው?
questions.explanation: ካሬ አራቱም ማዕዘኖቹ 90° ናቸው። ሲሊንደር ባለሦስት አቅጣጫ ቅርጽ ነው፤ ሮምቡስና ትራፔዞይድ ትክክለኛ ማዕዘን የግድ አይኖራቸውም። (ማስታወሻ፦ ይህ ጥያቄ ከተበላሸ ቅጂ በአዲስ መልክ ተጽፏል፤ ምስሉ ስላልተካተተ መምህር ከወረቀቱ ጋር ያመሳክረው።)

questions.subject: maths
questions.q: ከሚከተሉት ውስጥ የሬክታንግል (አራት ማዕዘን) ባሕርይ የሆነው የቱ ነው?
questions.explanation: የሬክታንግል ተቃራኒ ጎኖች ትይዩና እኩል ናቸው። አራቱም ጎኖች እኩል ቢሆኑ ካሬ ይሆናል፤ የአራት ማዕዘን የውስጥ አንግሎች ድምር 360° ነው። (ማስታወሻ፦ ይህ ጥያቄ ከተበላሸ ቅጂ በአዲስ መልክ ተጽፏል፤ ምስሉ ስላልተካተተ መምህር ከወረቀቱ ጋር ያመሳክረው።)

questions.subject: maths
questions.chapter: ምዕራፍ 3 — ስታትስቲክስ እና ተግባራዊ ችግሮች (Statistics & Applied Problems)
questions.q: የአንድ ቤተሰብ ወርሃዊ ወጪ በክብ ሰንጠረዥ (ፓይ ቻርት) ቀርቧል፦ ትምህርት 30°፣ ምግብ 120°፣ የቤት ኪራይ 90°፣ ሌሎች ወጪዎች 120°። ጠቅላላ ወርሃዊ ወጪው 6000 ብር ከሆነ ለምግብ የሚወጣው ስንት ብር ነው?
questions.explanation: ለምግብ የተሰጠው ክፍል 120° ነው፤ 120/360 = 1/3። ስለዚህ ወጪው 1/3 × 6000 = 2,000 ብር። (ማስታወሻ፦ ይህ ጥያቄ ከተበላሸ ቅጂ በአዲስ መልክ ተጽፏል፤ ምስሉ ስላልተካተተ መምህር ከወረቀቱ ጋር ያመሳክረው።)
